header.name: Theory of Computation
header.description: The course gives an overview over basic formal grammars and abstract machine models used in Computer Science. In particular, finite automata, pushdown automata, context-free grammars and Turing machines are studied with respect to  their properties and limits. Based on Turing machines the concepts of decidability and recursive enumerability are introduced.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: The student is able to describethe basic computational models FAs, PDAs, grammars and Turing machines.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: The student is able to formally model a given computational problem and prove its correctness.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: The student can explain the concepts of undecidability and recursive enumerability and is able to give examples of respective problems.

lecture_topics: Review of Discrete mathematics and machine models
Proving that certain languages are not regular
Reductions to prove undecidability of certain problems
